correctness.rationale: Hessian diagonalization decouples the dynamics. For one curvature mode \(q=\eta h\), the submitted state matrix has trace \(T=1+\alpha-q[1+\lambda(1-\alpha)]\) and determinant \(D=\alpha(1-q)\). The exact Jury expressions reduce to \(q(1-\alpha)(1+\lambda)\), \(2(1+\alpha)-q[(1+\alpha)+\lambda(1-\alpha)]\), and \(1-\alpha+\alpha q\); in the stated parameter range only the middle expression restricts stability. The largest curvature therefore gives the claimed iff threshold, and equality makes the characteristic polynomial vanish at \(-1\). The z-transform of the EMA gives \(A(-1)=1+\lambda(1-\alpha)/(1+\alpha)\), so the Nyquist expression is algebraically identical. The bundled randomized verifier corroborates the identities and the quoted numerical examples.
